questions.q: Which of the five account types is Revenue most closely related to, and why?
options: Assets, because revenue is always cash
Liabilities, because revenue is something the business owes
Equity, because revenue increases the owners' residual claim on the business
Expenses, because they are recorded the same way
questions.explain: Revenue increases equity (the business got richer by earning it), so revenue behaves like equity: credit-normal.

questions.q: What is the normal balance of an Asset account?
options: It depends on the day of the month
questions.explain: Assets are debit-normal: they increase with a debit and decrease with a credit.

questions.q: According to the DEAD mnemonic, which of these is debit-normal?
questions.explain: DEAD stands for Dividends, Expenses, Assets, Draws — all of these normally carry debit balances.

questions.q: Ashgrove Fixtures Inc. receives $5,000 cash for services performed. Which journal entry correctly records this?
questions.explain: Cash (an asset) increases, so it's debited. Service Revenue increases, so it's credited. Both move in their normal-balance direction.

questions.q: Why are Liabilities, Equity, and Revenue all credit-normal?
options: Because they are the least important accounts
Because credit-normal accounts are always larger in dollar amount
Because they all sit on the right-hand side of, or increase, the right-hand side of the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity)
There is no underlying reason; it is simply arbitrary tradition
questions.explain: Liabilities and Equity sit on the right side of the accounting equation and naturally increase on the credit side; Revenue increases Equity, so it behaves the same way.
